page.layout: One column of running text; no marginal notes. Page number and running head at the top; catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.p: loquium Virginis, vel non satis tempestive, vel non ad nutum oculi, fuerit admissus, satis graves hæ censebuntur injuriæ propter quas, si honoris & famæ prodigus esse nolis, adversarium ad singulare certamen provoces, vel conditiones congressus ab adversario oblatas non recuses. Intantum quidem, ut si vel ab amico, & familiari nonnulla passus sis, reparari illata nequeat injuria, nisi per infaustum duellum. Unde, etiam locus factus est proverbio : amicus es hodie, cras inimicus futurus.

Quinta occasio desumitur ab exemplo, quod utplurimum plus movet, quam res, aut ratio ipsa. Quia forte inter aulicos, quispiam gratus Principi, gratus Principis ministris, duello adversarium provocavit, ejus factum ad instar regulæ lesbiæ, ceteri omnes, ac-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "congressus" is printed with a glyph that looks like "cqngreffus"; read as congressus[?] in the text above was not marked, so it is noted here. The word "illata" has a worn final letter, read as illata. The printed "fi" and "fatis" and "cenfebuntur" use long s and are transcribed as si, satis, censebuntur. The printed "adverfarium" is transcribed as adversarium. The printed "proverbio :" keeps its space before the colon as printed.
